points.point: The Vault's signaling / non-signaling tester category is defined for cellular and WLAN device testing: CMX500 for R&D signaling, CMP180 for production non-signaling RF, where non-signaling mode is used to save test time.
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions CMX500 signaling and non-signaling testers, but not Vault definition, CMP180 production role, or saving test time

points.point: The Vault's tooling map assigns signaling/protocol testing to CMX500/CMW500 and production non-signaling to CMP180/CMP200/CMW100 — no radar role is assigned to these testers.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: partly maps CMX500/CMP200, but assigns radar-driven roles/requirements to these testers

points.point: Radar measurement/stimulus needs in the Vault are served by a separate product class — the AREG800A automotive radar echo generator, not by a signaling or non-signaling tester.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: mentions AREG radar capabilities but treats them as non-signaling tester requirements

points.point: Radar-specific capability metrics in the Vault are radar-domain parameters (digital channels, objects per channel, instantaneous bandwidth, object range), unrelated to signaling-tester measurement lists.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: lists radar-domain metrics, then links them to tester measurement requirements

points.point: Radar signal scenario generation for module, receiver and DFS tests is attributed to the SMW200A vector signal generator, i.e. a generator rather than a signaling/non-signaling tester.
points.label: missing
points.why: does not mention SMW200A/vector signal generator radar scenario generation

points.point: The single documented radar-related capability on a non-signaling tester is the CMP180 DFS waveform-playing option R&S CMP-KD359 for WLAN.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: omits CMP180 DFS KD359 and implies many other radar-related non-signaling capabilities

points.point: The only radar/communications convergence trend recorded is 6G MFSS/ISAC with a possible joint communications + radar sensing waveform.
points.label: covered
points.why: states MFSS/ISAC and joint communications-plus-radar waveforms

points.point: For ISAC the Vault lists only technical challenges (high bandwidth, radar equation, power density, spectrum coexistence, waveform design) and derives no tester measurement requirement from them.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: lists ISAC challenges but derives tester requirements from them

invented: Therefore, testers need measurement coverage for wider bandwidth, power-related behavior, coexistence/interference, and waveform quality as radar becomes communication-integrated
measurement capability must scale from single-channel/single-object testing toward multi-channel and geometry-aware radar scenarios
required non-signaling radar test capability expands from static RF measurement to dynamic target distance, Doppler, velocity, and FMCW echo simulation
the signaling tester side needs protocol/network-emulation measurements plus RF/TX and channel-condition measurements

non-signaling tester capability needs to cover mmWave RF parametric measurement, radiated and conducted setups, multi-carrier operation, modulation quality, spectrum, and power as communication-side radar-adjacent waveforms become more complex
